technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 (Azure Event Hubs), use Spring Cloud Stream binder pattern with Azure SDK for Java, implementing producer and consumer as Spring Boot auto-configuration.
For U2 (IPython Notebook integration), embed a REST service within Spring XD that exposes endpoints for interactive data computations, leveraging Jupyter kernel gateway if needed.

For U3 (upgrade preservation), implement a migration script that copies specified directories and configuration files ({{dirs}}/{{files}}, {{servers.yml}}) from old installation to new, with conflict handling.
For U4 (direct binding), extend Spring Cloud Stream's channel adapter to support direct method invocation or in-process event bus, bypassing message middleware, while maintaining existing API.
For U5 (REST API for xd-admin), use Spring MVC and Spring Data REST to expose CRUD endpoints for streaming and batch pipelines, with service layer abstraction.
For U6 (ModuleRegistry stubs), create mock implementations using Mockito and a simple in-memory registry for testing.
For U7 (move spring-cloud-stream-modules), use git filter-repo to preserve commit history while moving code to target repository, then update build and dependency references.
For U8 (in-memory stream definition repository), implement a concurrent HashMap-based repository that implements the existing repository interface, suitable for development mode only.
Overall architecture follows Spring Boot's auto-configuration and modularity; all new features are built as separate modules where appropriate.
assumptions: All development is performed by a single developer with full proficiency in Spring Framework, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring XD, and related ecosystems.
Existing codebases (Spring Framework, Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data) are available and fully functional in a local development environment.
No external dependencies require procurement or licensing; all used libraries are open-source and available via Maven Central.
Testing includes unit tests and integration tests using JUnit and Mockito; acceptance testing against real Azure Event Hubs instance is assumed to be possible.
Development effort is measured in net working days (8 hours), excluding overhead for meetings, code review by others, or deployment.
User stories are independent and can be implemented in parallel, but the developer works sequentially on each; no dependencies between stories affect effort.
Documentation for each feature is included in the development effort (e.g., technical documentation, usage guides).
The repository migration (U7) does not require coordinating with other teams or handling breaking changes for external consumers beyond updating import paths.

activities.activity_description: Design and implement a Spring Cloud Stream binder for Azure Event Hubs, including producer and consumer support, configuration, unit/integration tests, and documentation.
Develop integration for IPython/Jupyter notebooks within Spring XD, enabling interactive data computations via a REST API, including server-side logic and tests.
Create a migration mechanism to preserve existing installation directories and configuration files ({{dirs}}/{{files}}, {{servers.yml}}) during upgrade to latest Spring XD.

activities.activity_name: Direct Binding for Spring Cloud Stream (U4)
activities.activity_description: Implement an option for direct module binding without messaging middleware, reducing latency for high-throughput scenarios; includes core changes and tests.
Establish REST API endpoints for CRUD operations on streaming and batch pipelines in Spring Cloud Data, including controllers, services, and tests.
Create stub implementations for ModuleRegistry to enable mock streams for testing purposes, including unit tests.
Migrate the spring-cloud-stream-modules codebase from s-c-s to s-c repository, preserving git history, updating build files and references, and verifying tests.
Implement a non-persistent in-memory repository for stream definitions in Spring Cloud Data to simplify development, with tests.
Integrate all developed features, run end-to-end tests, fix integration issues, update overall documentation, and prepare release artifacts.
